item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 如何有效选到育儿有担当的男性 每一个男人都是有provider天性的，但是他们只会给自己深度认可的女性和她的孩子provide。牢牢记
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
如何有效选到育儿有担当的男性

每一个男人都是有provider天性的，但是他们只会给自己深度认可的女性和她的孩子provide。牢牢记住这句话，就不会乱找孩子爸。事业女性如果不幸被当成合伙aa过日子的话，如果没孩子，我甚至建议为了长远个人发展和事业，尽早离开，好好提升自己，找真正欣赏和珍惜自己的。

第一步，找恋爱约会时期就非常有付出意愿的且有财力的（缺一不可）。严格计较要aa的，要求你一顿我一顿的，吃饭约会只去二三十块人均，送了几十几百礼物马上要回去的等量的，只要沾到这种模式，怀孕生娃后，女生会非常后悔（事业，身体健康，颜值就别想了）。基本逻辑：恋爱时愿意付出的这笔钱，男性是有能力且很自然可以挪到月嫂和女生产后修复的，因为本来就是给女生用的。觉得女生值得且男性本身就有能力投入，才可能在育儿上尽可能减小女生负担。家务做饭完全外包，月嫂和丈夫一起帮忙，如果加上双方家长轮流过来帮忙，女生产后身材修复和基本休息会好非常多，主要事业也能保住，而且最关键的是这个模式会延续到孩子长大后（女生回归职场后）。

选错人的，一般就是女方妈妈+女方两个人带，月嫂不会有，最多aa，产后修复不用想，孩子大了之后也是全部女方来做，爸爸负责拍家庭照时入镜。除非女生天赋异禀，体能异禀，事业被影响概率太高，主要形象也会因为疲劳被影响，吸引力再一次被降低（本来aa说直白点，就是因为男生觉得女生形象不行，但是能过日子，所以内心勉为其难在一起了），会出问题（出轨和家暴，语言暴力和贬低是必定有），女生不要走到那一步。

所以简单粗暴的话，aa的直接筛了。让你感受到计较的或者付了钱就暗示欠了他要还的，直接筛，不会错的。付出意愿是最珍贵的，重要性大于财力。丁克当然随意，不涉及育儿的话，看自己高兴，我这里只说女生如何保证育儿后自己健康和事业能保住的择偶筛选。

第二步，走到结婚，找好律师，婚前协议写好育儿分配，白纸黑字法律生效。

第一步之前的第0步，请狠狠提升自己，再去婚恋。各个维度（颜值形象只是门票，职业，交流，生活品质，社交圈层），这样的男性要求是非常高的，选择权非常大，筛人是非常狠。初期只有0.1秒，0.1秒不过关，没有下一步。每一个下一步，都是tight game。能轻轻松松得来的，比如女生aa可以大幅度增大pool（但想找第一类靠aa，是没有任何优势的，因为他们唯独不在乎这点），日子到了育儿，会发现脑子严重进水。

别去看感觉，别去看“感觉这个人很可靠很老实”，别去看光环，别去看“我们是学生时代一起吃苦走上来的”（没一起过过好日子），这些都保证不了什么。

如果实在不行，直接走第二步，做不到的男性这婚前协议是不会愿意签的。

item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 经典老帖：《德国的中国学生很土气》 这是十多年前在新浪微博上掀起大量转发的一篇微博里截图的文章。事后原文很快被官网删了，但唯恐天下不乱
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
经典老帖：《德国的中国学生很土气》

这是十多年前在新浪微博上掀起大量转发的一篇微博里截图的文章。事后原文很快被官网删了，但唯恐天下不乱的婶子在微博上截屏了截屏……

官网原文发布日期:2012-06-22
点击数:786
我在英国留学，偶尔到德国，看到在德国和英国留学的中国人差别很大，在英国的很帅气，在德国的很土气。
英国是个绅士和淑女风度十足的国家，在英国留学的中国人也“沾染”上了这些“习气”，每到学校聚会，同学们总要着意打扮一番。男生们西装革履，女生们也要“浓妆淡抹总相宜”，“昂首挺胸“地招呼、谈吐,虽然知道是在“装腔作势”，可心中总是美滋滋的，享受着高雅的瞬间和情调。久而久之，对这样的英国式的社交就有了几分期待，社交活动也成了留学生涯中的美味。
这周有机会在德国参加了一场中国学生的聚会，其中也有些德国人和其他国家的人。很惊讶地看到，这里的中国学生很“土”，尤其是男生们，都穿着牛仔裤，上衣也多是皱褶满布，一看就知是很长时间没洗过，更不要说熨过了，似乎他们参加聚会就是要展示他们的還和不入流。女生的衣着也乏善可陈。大多数男女生共同的特点就是头发乱，说话声音很大，旁若无人，即便是主人还在招呼，他们也丝毫不在意。甚至，他们对主人走过身边时的欢迎和友好示意也不在意，握手的姿势十分委琐，一点都不气派，不舒展，透着“奴相”。更让人不解的是，主人走近时，有些学生居然赶快躲开，象小偷一样地钻进旁边的人堆中去。到吃饭的时候，情形近于“惨不忍睹”，不仅男生“狼吞虎咽”，就是女生也不少人端着食物摞出尖的盘子，全无淑女的样子。看到这些，一起从英国过来的同伴说：已经没有胃口。在德国参加的这场中国学生的聚会，让人很压抑，好像他们缺吃少衣,“温饱”是个大问题。
https://oss.1p3a.com/forum/202611/20/14310ljpz74dz1punfzcp.jpg
我一个朋友跟我说，小红书上（我没这app所以只能听他说），北美留学生是豪车海王绿茶婊的纠缠，德国留学生是售卖用剩下的半瓶酱油引起的纠纷…… 感叹当年的德国，打开了多少中国赤贫人家的孩子逆天改命进入中产阶级的门。如今的德国，机会不多了。

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.title: MacroMicro 🔏 Nvidia's purchase commitments across the AI ecosystem have climbed
item.description:
MacroMicro
🔏 Nvidia's purchase commitments across the AI ecosystem have climbed to $390B, up from $279B. Free cash flow nearly doubled to $43.78B in Q3, giving the company room to keep funding the expansion. But the balance sheet is taking on a growing role in financing the AI buildout.

Nvidia is increasingly acting as a financial intermediary across its customer and supplier network. Equity investments, cloud agreements, purchase commitments and loan guarantees are all part of the arrangement. The model keeps capital flowing through the ecosystem, with money eventually returning to Nvidia as GPU orders.

The question is how much of this financing depends on customers actually getting their data centers online. CoreWeave, for example, has 3.1GW of contracted capacity, but only around 1.1GW is energized. Its ability to convert contracted capacity into revenue depends heavily on power availability and construction timelines.

That puts the next phase of the AI trade under a different set of pressures. Chip demand remains strong, but the financing structure supporting that demand deserves closer scrutiny.

In this week's commentary, we trace Nvidia's financial exposure through its guarantees, customer commitments and Neocloud relationships, alongside the borrowing costs and power deployment data that could reveal emerging credit stress. We also examine Anthropic's $1.5T IPO and the compute economics behind its path to profitability, as well as what the Fed's increasingly hawkish stance means for markets heading into December.

🔗 Full report: https://t.co/vT4mA6qt9a

item.title: Daily Dose of Data Science Why temperature 0 isn't deterministic in LLM inferenc
item.description:
Daily Dose of Data Science
Why temperature 0 isn't deterministic in LLM inference?

(a popular technical LLM interview question)

At temperature 0, inference engines usually switch to greedy decoding directly. At every step, they pick the highest-logit token, so the same prompt should give the same output every time.

In practice, it doesn't.

Thinking Machines actually tested this by sending "Tell me about Richard Feynman" to Qwen3-235B 1,000 times at temperature 0 and got 80 unique completions.

While picking the biggest logit is a perfectly deterministic step...

...the variation actually comes from computing the logits themselves. If those numbers come out slightly different, argmax can pick a different token.

Let's understand how the logits can slightly change at times.

1) The order of addition changes the result:

GPUs store numbers with limited precision. fp16 keeps only 11 significant bits, and between 1024 and 2048, that leaves no room for anything after the decimal point. So 1024.4 gets rounded back to 1024.

Now consider 1024 + 0.4 + 0.4 in two orders.

Left to right, 1024 + 0.4 rounds back to 1024, and adding 0.4 again rounds back to 1024. The answer is 1024.

If the small numbers go first, 0.4 + 0.4 gives 0.8, and 1024 + 0.8 rounds up to 1025. The answer is 1025.

An LLM performs billions of such additions in every forward pass, so if their order changes, the logits change slightly too.

2) What causes the order to change?

The popular reason is that parallel GPU threads finish in an unpredictable order.

But that isn't the main reason, since the kernels in a typical forward pass compute each sum in a fixed order.

So the same matrix multiplication on the same inputs, at the same batch size, gives bit-for-bit identical results every time.

3) The real reason is the other requests on the server:

An inference server groups requests from many users into a batch and runs them together.

The kernels decide how to split their work based on the batch size.

- With a large batch, every GPU core is busy, so each core computes its sum in one go.

- With a small batch, many cores would sit idle, so the kernel cuts each long sum into chunks, spreads them across cores, and combines the partial results at the end.

A different split leads to a different order of addition, and the batch size depends on how many other people are using the server at that moment.

4) How this tiny difference changes the entire answer:

Consider two runs of the same prompt:

In a batch of 8, say the logits come out as:
- "Queens" = 12.3417
- "New" = 12.3415

In this case, argmax picks "Queens".

In a batch of 32, the rounding works out slightly differently, giving:
- "Queens" = 12.3414
- "New" = 12.3416

In this case, argmax picks "New".

The output only flips at such near ties. And every token after that is generated from a different prefix.

In the above test by Thinking Machines, all 1,000 runs matched for the first 102 tokens. At token 103, 992 runs wrote "Queens, New York" while 8 wrote "New York City".

5) The solution:

This isn't a big problem per se, but to make it genuinely deterministic, every kernel should split its work the same way regardless of batch size (for attention, that means a fixed chunk size), even if it leaves some cores idle.

Thinking Machine tested this with batch-invariant kernels, where all 1,000 runs were identical. But this impacted speed.

On Qwen3-8B, default vLLM took 26s for 1,000 requests, while the deterministic version took 55s, and 42s after an improved attention kernel.

The visual below depicts what we discussed.

That said, batching isn't the only thing that changes how these sums get split.

A cache hit does too, since some attention kernels process cached tokens separately from new ones, and Thinking Machines had to handle this case explicitly.

We previously covered the four caches in LLM serving in an article, with code for each.

Read it below.
